transcript:
Sarah (Sales): Last time you mentioned that you were considering deployment across three factories. Is that still the plan?
Anna Keller: Yes. The first factory is basically approved internally. The main question is whether we can justify expanding to all three this year.
Sarah: What's preventing that decision?
Anna Keller: Mostly pricing. If we deploy at all three locations, procurement expects a better price than what is currently in the proposal.
Markus Vogel: From my side, I also still need confirmation regarding SSO and data residency.
Sarah: If we solve those security questions and restructure the pricing for three factories, would there be anything else blocking approval?
Anna Keller: Probably not. I think we could take it to procurement after that.
Sarah: Great. I'll send a three-year pricing option and the security documentation. Can we review it together next Tuesday?
Anna Keller: Yes, that works.

Michael (Sales): What would make this pilot successful for you?
Eva de Vries: Forecast accuracy is the main thing. Our managers don't trust the current forecast.
Tom Smit: We also have a lot of custom opportunity fields in the CRM. If your connector ignores those, the dashboard won't be useful.
Michael: We can map custom fields. Would you be comfortable defining three or four success metrics before the pilot starts?
Eva de Vries: Yes. Forecast accuracy, pipeline coverage, conversion by stage, and probably manager adoption.
Michael: And if the pilot improves those metrics?
Eva de Vries: Then I can make the case for rolling it out to the entire sales organization.

Rachel (Sales): Before we finalize the proposal, are there any technical blockers left?
Mette Nielsen: The architecture looks fine now. My concern was whether you could integrate without creating another isolated data store.
Rachel: The design uses your existing platform and keeps the source systems authoritative.
Mette Nielsen: That's what we needed.
Lars Jensen: For me the bigger question is rollout. I don't want this to become a one-business-unit experiment.
Rachel: We can structure the contract around a phased rollout, but price it as an enterprise agreement.
Lars Jensen: Good. If security signs off and the rollout plan is included, I think we can move forward.
Mette Nielsen: From the technical side, I can recommend approval.

Daniel (Sales): The team seemed positive about the solution. What's stopping the project?
Camille Martin: The product isn't the issue. Finance froze most discretionary spending for the rest of the year.
Daniel: Would reducing the project scope help?
Camille Martin: Probably not. The bigger problem is that this isn't considered critical compared with our other initiatives.
Daniel: Is there anything we could provide to strengthen the case?
Camille Martin: A stronger ROI model would help next time, but it won't unlock budget this year.
Daniel: Should we revisit it during next year's planning cycle?
Camille Martin: Yes. Contact me around October when we start planning next year's budget.

Laura (Sales): What is driving the project internally?
Noah Frei: We have too many fragmented analytics pipelines. Analysts spend a lot of time preparing data instead of analyzing it.
Sofia Meier: I agree with the problem, but procurement will need very clear implementation milestones and fixed costs.
Laura: If we can show a staged implementation with fixed milestones, would that address the procurement concern?
Sofia Meier: Partly. Payment terms also matter. Annual prepayment will be difficult for us.
Laura: Would quarterly payments make approval easier?
Sofia Meier: Yes, definitely.
Noah Frei: From my side, the technical value is clear. The main question is commercial structure.

Chris (Sales): You mentioned automation is a priority. Which process causes the most pain today?
Louise Dubois: That's actually what we're still trying to determine. There are many manual processes.
Arthur Peeters: Shipment exception handling is probably the best candidate. The team spends hours coordinating exceptions by email.
Chris: Who owns that process?
Arthur Peeters: Operations, but we should bring the regional operations manager into the next meeting.
Louise Dubois: Before we discuss software, I want a clear business case around one process.
Chris: Understood. We'll focus the next workshop on shipment exceptions and quantify the current manual effort.

Emma (Sales): Are there any remaining concerns besides commercial terms?
James Carter: Model governance is mostly resolved. The documentation Priya reviewed was sufficient.
Priya Shah: Yes. We still want lineage and monitoring included in the implementation plan, but I don't see that as a blocker.
Emma: On pricing, what would make a multi-year commitment work?
James Carter: The current price is acceptable for one year. For three years, I need a meaningful incentive.
Emma: Would a lower effective annual price plus price protection address that?
James Carter: Potentially. Show me both a two-year and a three-year option.
Emma: If one of those works commercially, are we ready for legal review?
James Carter: Yes.

Maria (Sales): Is there anything preventing you from moving ahead with the starter package?
Erik Lind: Not really. I want to keep deployment simple and start before the end of October.
Sara Berg: I still need clarity on the implementation fee.
Maria: We can include implementation in the first-year subscription instead of charging it separately.
Sara Berg: That would simplify approval.
Erik Lind: If you can confirm the October deployment slot, send us the final order form.
Maria: I can confirm that today.
Erik Lind: Then I think we're ready.

Rachel (Sales): What would you need to see before expanding the AI optimization module?
Lars Jensen: I need evidence that it affects either energy output or operating cost. Ideally both.
Mette Nielsen: Technically, I'd prefer not to deploy across the whole fleet immediately.
Rachel: What about a proof of value on one wind farm?
Mette Nielsen: That's exactly what I was thinking.
Lars Jensen: If the proof shows measurable impact, expansion becomes much easier to approve.
Rachel: Let's agree on the baseline metrics before we start.
Lars Jensen: Good. Then the result is something I can take directly to the investment committee.

Chris (Sales): Arthur has been positive about the platform, but he mentioned sponsorship might be an issue.
Louise Dubois: That's correct. I like the concept, but we have two transformation programs that already have executive backing.
Chris: Is there a smaller scope that you could sponsor?
Louise Dubois: Not this year. It's less about scope and more about organizational priority.
Arthur Peeters: Could we keep the technical work alive and revisit budget later?
Louise Dubois: We can revisit it next planning cycle, but I don't want the team spending more time on it now.
Chris: Understood. We'll close the opportunity for now and reconnect during planning.
